extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks to evaluate mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MATHVISTA: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). Existing datasets were collected by reviewing more than 70 datasets and selecting 28 that contain math-related instances. New datasets were created to address gaps in logical reasoning on puzzle test diagrams, statistical reasoning on functional plots, and scientific reasoning on academic figures.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). IQTest sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms. FunctionQA emphasizes functional plots. PaperQA sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure a balanced representation of each source in the final compiled benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset is divided into two subsets: testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples). A sampling strategy was adopted for testmini: (1) randomly sample questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset; (2) randomly sample the remaining questions for each source dataset on its proportion in the entire set. Several quality checks were conducted to address any unidentified errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For VQA datasets, three expert annotators manually labeled examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning using majority voting. For the three new datasets, questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. Initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. Metadata (question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context) was annotated. Mathematical reasoning categories were automatically labeled and verified by expert annotators on 1,000 examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For the new datasets, inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% was achieved; among 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements. For VQA labeling, Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 was achieved among three annotators. For mathematical reasoning category labeling, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations had the exact same set of reasoning types, while 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields; Expert annotators
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning (numeric answers or quantity words); Automatic annotation for the labeling of mathematical reasoning
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for test will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and we will maintain an online evaluation platform. We are committed to maintaining the datasets, such as refining the potential data noise, in response to the community feedback. Also, we are committed to evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: This significant gap underscores the critical role that MATHVISTA will play in the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks. AI agents with strong mathematical reasoning capabilities in visual contexts have a wide range of real-world applications, such as solving complex problems in educational disciplines, helping analysts with logical queries about statistical data, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: While MATHVISTA encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The dataset’s focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, necessitates a more labor-intensive process for collecting high-quality data compared to textual-only or general-purpose datasets. Thus, the scalability and generalizability of our benchmark to other domains remain a concern.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: One limitation is the dataset coverage. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure. Our study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models.
